title: Navigating Our Future Together Means Leaving No One Behind
summary: Hindi matatawag na tunay na pag-unlad ang anumang pagsulong na nakakamit kapalit ng karapatan at kapakanan ng mamamayan.
byline: Jana Mikaela Delgado Principe, Arianna Shay Zafra, MJ Legaspi

blocks.text: The right of our Filipino people to speak, to assemble, and to disagree are not negotiable; it is a right enshrined in the Constitution and a necessary foundation of a truly just society. One that serves all citizens, and not just a select few.

As the Philippines hosts the 49th ASEAN Summit and welcomes United States President Donald Trump, we keep in mind that every Filipino voice must be respected and protected. We call on the authorities to honor the due process and protect fundamental civil liberties in light of what happened November 15—students and advocates and members of the press were arrested and scattered all over Metro Manila and Cebu.

From university campuses to the streets, these are our people—those who voiced concerns for the marginalized groups fearing for their lands and livelihoods, and who spoke out against Trump’s visit and the US-led Pax Silica initiative. However, they were met not with answers, but with force from those who swore to protect the Filipino people, even detaining student journalists and effectively preventing the youth from doing what a free press was always meant to do.

But worries about Pax Silica go beyond political differences. Indigenous communities have cautioned about possible displacement of their populations, expropriation of ancestral lands and the environmental fallout that can come from large-scale industrial development. These are not minor considerations that can simply be dismissed in the name of modernization.

We still value those things, but we have to look closer: is this really progress, or are we just enforcing compliance? How easy it is to frame all this in the name of respect and decorum, for innovation and advancement.

Our people are being forced into a false choice between innovation and justice. But progress must be collective, not selective. Progress is not progress if it leaves people behind. Development is not sustainable if it destroys the very communities, cultures, and ecosystems it is supposed to serve.

And yet, this is the exact type of development our government is pushing. As an organization that advocates for the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, we believe development must be inclusive, equitable, and sustainable.

While the Philippines signed the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in 2015, the government continues to be selective in which goals it honors, overlooking that human rights and sustainable development are indivisible. The SDGs call for strong institutions, climate action, reduced inequalities, and the protection of life on land. These commitments mean little if the very people advocating for these causes face intimidation for making their stances heard.

At the same time, this year’s ASEAN theme, ‘Navigating Our Future, Together,’ emphasizes collective action and shared progress. Moving forward together requires ensuring that no community is excluded, no voice is disregarded, and no one is left behind. Solidarity must extend beyond international commitments and be reflected in how people are protected at home, starting with the very institutions tasked with keeping them safe.

The Philippine National Police and other law enforcement institutions must remain accountable to the public and uphold their fundamental mandate to serve and protect. Their actions must reflect respect for human rights and due process, regardless of the affiliations or causes of those exercising their rights.
The protection of Indigenous Peoples, the dignity of ordinary Filipinos, and the right to peaceful expression must remain central to any commitment to democracy and sustainable development.

Hindi matatawag na tunay na pag-unlad ang anumang pagsulong na nakakamit kapalit ng karapatan at kapakanan ng mamamayan. Hindi rin tunay na pagkakaisa kung ang mga tinig ng mga katutubo at ordinaryong Pilipinong ipinaglalaban ang kanilang mga karapatan ay binabalewala o hindi pinakikinggan. Ang kinabukasan ng bansa ay hindi dapat pinagpapasiyahan nang hindi kinikilala ang karapatan ng sambayanan na magkaroon ng tinig at makilahok sa mga desisyong direktang nakaaapekto sa kanilang buhay at kinabukasan.
